body: Arts and Culture Commission - Special Meeting
agenda_text:
AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION - SPECIAL MEETING
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Library,
Arts and Culture Department, at (818) 548-2030, during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  DECEMBER 8, 2022 AT 9:00 AM

  1.  SPECIAL BUSINESS AGENDA – 9:00 AM
  Roll Call
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the December 8, 2022
  Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission was Posted on
  December 1, 2022 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

  2.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
   Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.

3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal

  Arts & Culture Administrator

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.

 5.  ACTION ITEMS
  a. Arts and Culture Commission – Meeting Date/Time

  1. Motion rescinding the Commission’s October 20, 2022 Motion recommending that the
  City Council approve the rescheduling of the Commission’s Regular Meeting from the 3rd
  Thursday of each month, 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM, to the 2nd Thursday of each month, 9:00
  AM – 11:00 AM.
  2. Resolution repealing Resolution No. 2014-01 related to Commission Rules of Procedure
  and adopting new Rules of Procedure that:
  (a) Reschedule the date and time of the Arts and Culture Commission’s Regular
  Meeting to the 2nd Thursday of each month, 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM; and
  (b) Revise the order of business on Agendas, moving Written Communications to
  Agenda Item 4, immediately followed by Agenda Item 5: Oral Communications, in
  alignment with the City Council meeting agenda.

  b. City-Wide Public Art RFP: Central Park Groundlevel Sculpture
  1. Motion directing staff to invite the artist finalists for the Central Park Groundlevel
  Sculpture public art to modify their proposed design rendering to enable the placement
  of their art piece at an alternate location within Central Park; and approving the issuance
  of an additional stipend to the artists, in an amount not to exceed $200.00 per artist
  dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund, for redesigning the proposed artwork.

6.  DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2022-2023 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Culmination
  ii. Mural Ordinance – Update
  iii. Creative Crosswalks – Update
  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS- No Update
  3. PERFORMING ARTS
  i. 2023 Performance Series Application – Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update
  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS
  i. PR Firm RFP – Update
 7.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

8.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

9.  ADJOURNMENT
  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is January 12, 2023,
  at 10:00 AM in City Council Chambers (613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor).
minutes_text:
CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Special Meeting
  AMENDED

  Thursday, December 8, 2022 at 9:00 a.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on December 8, 2022, at 9:00 a.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Tufenkian, Vidor, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  •  Absent: Commissioner Zadorian
  •  The Agenda for the December 8, 2022, Special Meeting was posted on December 1, 2022, on the
  Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS

  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal Arts & Culture
  Administrator
  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts &
  Culture locations.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes. Members of
  the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the Speaker, but there will be no Debate or
  Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  – None

5. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. Arts and Culture Commission – Meeting Date/Time
  1. Motion rescinding the Commission’s October 20, 2022, Motion recommending that the City Council
  approve the rescheduling of the Commission’s Regular Meeting from the 3rd Thursday of each
  month, 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM, to the 2nd Thursday of each month, 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM.
  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby RESCINDS its October 20, 2022, Motion
  recommending that the City Council approve the rescheduling of the Commission’s Regular Meeting
  from the 3rd Thursday of each month, 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM, to the 2nd Thursday of each month, 9:00
  AM – 11:00 PM, for the reasons more fully explained in the December 8, 2022, Report by the
  Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Moved:  Commissioner Viar
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Vidor, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  1
   2. Resolution repealing Resolution No. 2014-01 related to Commission Rules of Procedure and adopting
  new Rules of Procedure that:
  (a) Reschedule the date and time of the Arts and Culture Commission’s Regular Meeting to the 2nd
  Thursday of each month, 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM; and

  (b) Revise the order of business on Agendas, moving Written Communications to Agenda Item 4,
  immediately followed by Agenda Item 5: Oral Communications, in alignment with the City Council
  meeting agenda.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby reschedule the date and time of the Arts and
  Culture Commission’s Regular Meeting to the 2nd Thursday of each month, 10:00 AM – 12:00
  PM; and Revise the order of business on Agendas, moving Written Communications to Agenda
  Item 4, immediately followed by Agenda Item 5: Oral Communications, in alignment with the City
  Council meeting agenda.

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded:  Commissioner Viar

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Vidor, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

b.  City-Wide Public Art RFP: Central Park Groundlevel Sculpture
  1. Motion directing staff to invite the artist finalists for the Central Park Groundlevel Sculpture public art to
  modify their proposed design rendering to enable the placement of their art piece at an alternate
  location within Central Park; and approving the issuance of an additional stipend to the artists, in an
  amount not to exceed $200.00 per artist dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund, for
  redesigning the proposed artwork.
  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a brief summary of the proposed project; Commission asked
  questions and gave their input.
  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby directs staff to invite the artist finalists for the Central
  Park Ground level Sculpture public art to modify their proposed design rendering to enable the
  placement of their art piece at an alternate location within Central Park, as more fully explained in
  the December 8, 2022 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator;
  and approves the issuance of an additional stipend to the artists, in an amount not to exceed
  $ 200.00 per artist dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund, for redesigning the proposed
  artwork.

  Moved:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  Seconded:  Commissioner Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Vidor, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  2
 6. DISCUSSION ITEM(s) / REPORT(s)
  a. 2022-2023 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Culmination
  • Staff hosted a Projects Culmination/Celebration Reception on Saturday, December 3, 2022,
  12:00PM – 2:00PM at the Museum of Neon Art, to celebrate the 17 artists and their projects.
  • Chair Yank, Commissioners Viar and Vidor thanked Dr. Shaffer, Ms. Fukutomi- Jones and
  staff for organizing and hosting a Project Culmination reception for the City-Wide Arts: Art
  Happens Anywhere artists on Saturday December 3rd at the museum of Neon Art

  ii. Mural Ordinance – Update
  •  Staff is working with Ms. Odenkirk and the draft Mural Ordinance and Policies, and
  Procedures will be scheduled for initial review by the Commission at an upcoming Regular
  Meeting.

  iii. Creative Crosswalks – Update
  •  On November 29, 2022, during the City Council Meeting, City Council approved the designs
  and Staff will be working with the Public Works and the artists to tentatively install the
  crosswalk murals some time in February/March 2023.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS- No Update

  3. PERFORMING ARTS
  i.  2023 Performance Series Application – Update
  • Staff opened the 2023 Performance Series application intended for music ensembles to
  perform as part of the 222 East Concert Series and Brand Summer Music Series. The
  application is currently open and closes on January 27, 2023, at 5:00 pm. Artists are
  encouraged to apply.

  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update

  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS
  i.  PR Firm RFP – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi- Jones stated that five proposals were received, and staff narrowed it down to
  three proposals. She stated that staff will move forward in doing internal interviews in late
  December and staff will have the finalists present in January to the Commission.

7. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  •  Commissioner Tufenkian thanked staff and Commission for their hard work.
  •  Commissioner Viar addressed Dr. Shaffer and Ms. Fukutomi-Jones and all the Library Arts
  and Culture staff who work on Arts and Culture Commission projects and thanked staff for
  their time and effort and thanked all her fellow Commissioners for expanding her knowledge
  of art and wished everyone Happy Holidays.
  •  Commissioner Vidor stated she wanted to add her voice to all the compliments
  Commissioner Viar gave to staff and stated she appreciated her fellow commissioners and
  the whole community of artists and art institutions in the city of Glendale.
  •  Commissioner Yank stated that she’s worked in Art administration nonprofits for about 20
  years and this is her first experience behind the scenes and witnessing the growth of a
  municipal arts program that is robust and city-wide and stated she’s learned so much, it’s
  difficult because its government and its serves the people, it is both down in the nitty gritty
  and also holding a much larger vision as well as dealing with artists who may not have

  3
   worked with government or with the city before in producing their art work. She also stated
  that staff has done tremendous, ambitious, incredible job with the resources at hand. She
  thanked everyone for their efforts and stated it’s been a great pleasure to work with
  everyone.
  •  Dr Shaffer thanked the Commission for their volunteer services and stated that every time a
  commissioner shows up to an event its coming from a special place in their heart because
  they don’t have to be there but it is appreciated. He also stated that staff gave a preview
  showing to City Council of She Loves Collective art installation, and he was really moved
  by it and encourages everyone to go out and see it. Dr. Shaffer also thanked Ms. Fukutomi-
  Jones for making it all happen, he welcomed David to the Commission, and mentioned that
  Michael Grant said his goodbyes at the last Commission meeting. He thanked the
  Commission for their effort and their service.
  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones echoed Dr. Shaffer’s words and stated she really appreciated the
  Commission’s phenomenal work and vision because without it, staff could not implement it.
  She thanked the Commission for their vision and creating an Arts destination for Glendale
  and stated it is always a pleasure to work and always inspired and learning from each one of
  the Commissioners and is looking forward to working with the Commission next year and
  wished everyone Happy Holidays.

8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS- None
9. ADJOURNMENT 9:28 AM
The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is January 12, 2023, at 10:00 a.m., in City
Council Chambers (2nd Floor), 613 E. Broadway.
